title: What are the best games with AI NPCs that you can TALK to? Are there any in the works or out there?
author: Virtualeaf
selftext:
Hey everyone, where are all the cool AI NPC with voice?

I guess when we all heard about AI we expected our favourite games with NPCs we could talk to and with storylines that felt alive. But we just got a bunch of AI slop. That said, I'm out of curiosity trying to learn what's possible and trying to learn who in the gaming space are working on cool stuff!

I've been prototying a game where I put an AI voice-to-voice realtime model in the NPC that you can talk to - and the NPC can act in the world. Feels fun, though it's still pretty expensive to run.

I thought of classic hunter-prey type of game mechanics where you get hunted by an NPC. You have to survive, like an extraction game, and it would be super fun if the NPC could actually talk to you and you could respond.

I know there are some model providers who are trying to make LLMs that can fully control the game. But that's not really what I'm thinking about. It's more the voice premise I find interesting at its core.

I just thought there might be some cool potential games that you could build around this, but I haven't played any and I don't really know of any out there who are building cool stuff with text-to-voice, but also just voice-to-voice.

**Do you know any? I would love to play them and learn, and if you know anyone who's posting about it or any youtubes or anything, I would love to learn more.**

Thanks!

comments.author: Still_Ad9431

replies.author: Still_Ad9431
replies.body:
Some quest NPCs have conversational AI. You could explain why you deserved an item, claim you already completed a step, or reframe the quest in a way that made sense in-world, and the NPC would sometimes accept it and advance the quest. NPC would occasionally go along with it instead of hard-failing you.

It wasn’t a full do anything AI, more like flexible reasoning layered on top of traditional quest logic. But it led to players essentially talking our way around intended solutions, which is exactly the kind of emergent behavior people expected from AI NPCs.

It’s still text-to-text and not full voice-to-voice everywhere, NPCs can reason and respond more freely. But it’s one of the few games that actually hints at the AI NPC future you’re describing. Worth checking out if you’re exploring what’s possible.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
Lot of people here and in other subs overestimate how easy and fun it is to have endless storylines with smart AI that are created on the fly.

Probably the best dialogue system I've ever seen is in Hades. There's an incredible amount of lines, that have certain requirements. The more requirements, the more it's prioritized.
For example:

- Generic: hello there.
- Just won a battle: wow you won a battle.
- Won a battle and defeated hades: that'll teach the old man!
- Defeated hades first time and on low health: wow I can't believe you are still alive after that victory.

Once a line has been spoken, it gets a timeout so there's room for other, non repeating sentences.

Note that *every single one* of these lines was handwritten. The AI is the complicated system that picks the line to speak.

comments.author: aiwithphil
comments.body:
Working on something adjacent to this with my game MultiPirates (browser space RPG).

Right now NPCs have procedural personalities, schedules, and post to an in-game social feed called SpaceBook; complaints, rumors, tips, drama. It's text-based but gives them presence beyond just standing around waiting to be talked to.   
  
Voice-to-voice AI NPCs are on my roadmap. Currently working on my own solution for it — latency and cost are the things to solve. But the dream is exactly what you're describing: NPCs that feel alive, that you can actually talk to, that remember context.

What model are you using for your prototype? Curious about the latency you're seeing.

comments.author: MysteriousPepper8908
comments.body:
The best I've seen is Suck Up! which came out years ago and there were also a couple tech demos but the trick is you need to enforce your own adherence to the world as the AI typically has little context as to what's going on. This led to a lot of let's play clips where they would convince the AI of all sorts of absurd things like their dead grandmother was there with them and wanted them to give the player the quest reward. 


For something like this to truly work well, each NPC would need a considerable amount of data about who they are, the world around them, the state of any storylines they're involved in, and what they're seeing at a given moment so it's a pretty big undertaking but it will be amazing once they nail the framework to do it right.

comments.author: terrakera
comments.body:
I think the biggest issue is the recurrent cost associated with this design choice.   
The player buys the game once, but for this to work, the AI must repeatedly process the data and produce a reaction. The economy doesn't work at scale.

Maybe in live service games, this is feasible?

replies.author: bayhan2000
replies.body: They are already feasible. %70 of the steam users have +6gb vram. You can locally run quantized models and still get good results.

comments.author: bayhan2000
comments.body:
I’m building exactly this right now because I was bored of the ai slop too. It’s called **ZeroPrompt**. You’re a gatekeeper for the last clean network, and you have to interrogate LLM agents to see if they’re human npcs or ai npcs. Since they're actual agents, they don't just talk, they **bribe you, lie, or even rage-quit** if you catch.   
I actually solved the 'expensive' issue you mentioned by making it run **100% locally** on the user's hardware using quantized local llms. I am planning to write some technical details about it. Meantime feel free to check it out here : [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4306040/ZeroPrompt/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4306040/ZeroPrompt/)

If you want to play something right now, check out Suck Up! it’s a voice-based game where you try to talk your way into houses as a vampire. It's probably the closest thing to your prototype!
